Goals: - An AI can discover what meshanvil can do without reading Python source.
- An AI can decide the next safe command from one status response.
- An AI can list and read reports through a stable CLI contract instead of filesystem conventions.
- JSON output stays parseable and stable across locales.
- The human CLI remains friendly and unchanged unless `--json` is requested.
Key product decisions: - Keep this as CLI plus JSON. Agents get a dependable command surface, not a new runtime.
- Machine identifiers and error codes are stable and untranslated; human messages can stay localized.
- Advice is a read-only field of `status`, not its own command: it reports safe next steps and never performs them.
Overview: Makes meshanvil usable by AI operators through an explicit schema command, a single status view that also advises the next safe command, report access commands, stable JSON errors and a short agent playbook in `AGENTS.md`, without adding an agent runtime.

ai_context.keywords: agent CLI, JSON contract, schemas, status, reports, stable errors
ai_context.skip when: changing viewer presentation, geometry operations, packaging, or human-only CLI text.
ai_context.summary: Define meshanvil's AI-facing CLI contract: schema discovery, status, report access, stable JSON errors and a short agent playbook.
ai_context.use when: making meshanvil safer or easier for AI tools to operate through the command line.

Acceptance criteria: - AC1: `meshanvil schema --json` prints one object keyed `report`, `operation` and `cli`, describing the report shape, the operation manifest shape and the JSON envelopes well enough for an AI to validate them without reading Python source. One command, not three subcommands.

- AC2: `meshanvil status --json` prints one JSON object containing project identity, setup state, operation summary, report summary, viewer hint, and ordered next-action hints (reason code + command, advice only); stdout contains no human preamble.

- AC3: `meshanvil reports --json`, `meshanvil reports --latest --json`, and `meshanvil reports <id> --json` let an agent list reports, find the latest report, and read one report without walking the runtime reports directory itself.

- AC4: Every command that accepts `--json` returns the same top-level success and error envelope: success includes `ok: true`; failures include `ok: false`, `exit_code`, and a stable `error.code` plus a human `error.message`.

- AC5: Refusals that an agent can act on have stable error codes, at least for unknown operation, missing source file, engine missing, target busy, invalid parameter, malformed `--set`, unreadable input format, and unavailable work directory.

- AC6: `run --json` returns the report as machine data, not a stdout blob: at least `report_path`, `id` and the report `status`. Every `--json` command writes the envelope and nothing else to stdout; human and diagnostic text goes to stderr.
Needs: - The CLI now has `--json` on the most useful commands for automation, but an AI still has to infer too much from scattered commands and report files. A first-time agent needs one canonical way to learn the project state, the available schemas, the reports that already exist, and what to do next.

- `doctor --json`, `list --json`, `prune --json` and `run --json` do not yet share one error envelope. Refusals still expose translated human text as the only stable value in some paths, which makes an agent parse prose instead of identifiers.

- Reports are deliberately JSON files under the runtime reports directory, but there is no CLI for listing, selecting or reading them. Agents can read the filesystem, but that makes the workflow depend on filename conventions rather than a product contract.

- The report and operation formats are mostly discoverable by reading code, manifests and examples. That is workable for a human contributor and brittle for an AI operator, which should be able to ask the tool for the schema it is expected to obey.

- There is no single `status` command that answers whether the active directory is a project, whether setup passes, whether reports exist, which operations are available, and what the next safe command is.
- There is no short agent-oriented document that states the canonical commands, the `--json` preference, the report-first workflow, the `work/in` immutability rule, and how to attach Logics evidence.

ai_context.keywords: schema command, report schema, operation schema, CLI envelope
ai_context.skip when: validating historical reports or changing report semantics.
ai_context.summary: Add one `schema --json` command so agents can learn report, operation manifest and CLI JSON shapes from meshanvil itself.

Acceptance criteria: - AC1: `schema --json` prints one JSON object to stdout with the `report`, `operation` and `cli` keys and no human preamble.
- AC2: The `report` section names required top-level report fields and the optional sections the viewer consumes.
- AC3: The `operation` section names required manifest fields, parameter field shapes and known parameter types.
- AC4: The `cli` section describes the success envelope, error envelope, the stable error codes and the exit codes.
- AC5: `make check` fails if `schema --json` stops producing parseable JSON or drops a key.
Problem: - An agent has to infer the report, operation and CLI JSON shapes from source code and examples, which makes integration brittle and version-dependent.

ai_context.keywords: status json, preflight, project state, report summary
ai_context.skip when: adding operation execution, report mutation or viewer startup behavior.
ai_context.summary: Add one JSON preflight command that combines project, setup, operations, report summary, viewer hint and next hints.
ai_context.use when: implementing `meshanvil status --json` or shared status collection.

Acceptance criteria: - AC1: `status --json` prints one parseable object with `ok`, `project`, `doctor`, `operations`, `reports`, `viewer` and `next` keys.
- AC2: The command exits with the same refused status as `doctor` when required setup is missing, while still printing the JSON object.
- AC3: Report summary includes count and latest report id/path when present, but does not read every large artefact.
- AC4: Next-action hints are ordered, deterministic for the same project state, and include stable reason codes.
- AC5: `status --json` is read-only: it never writes under `work/`, starts a server, launches an engine or writes a report.
- AC6: Selfcheck covers a healthy project, an unhealthy project, and a project with no reports.
Problem: - A first-time agent must call several commands and inspect files to know whether it is in a project, whether setup passes, what operations exist, and whether reports already exist.

ai_context.keywords: reports json, latest report, report id, work ops
ai_context.skip when: changing report filenames, report contents or artefact opening.
ai_context.summary: Add report listing, latest-report and report-by-id CLI access so agents do not walk `work/ops` directly.

Acceptance criteria: - AC1: Report listing includes id, operation, status, path, input path when present, output path/state when present, and created/readable timestamp if available.
- AC2: Latest report resolution is deterministic and matches current filename ordering rules.
- AC3: Reading a report by id returns exactly one report or a stable ambiguous/not-found error.
- AC4: Malformed report files are reported in the listing with a stable warning field rather than crashing the command.
- AC5: Selfcheck covers empty, malformed, single-report and ambiguous-id cases.
Problem: - Reports are the product's main record, but agents must currently walk `work/ops` and understand filename conventions to find or read them.

ai_context.keywords: JSON envelope, ok false, exit code, error object, run report path, stdout discipline
ai_context.skip when: changing process exit codes or localized human messages.
ai_context.summary: Put every JSON-mode command on one success/error envelope while preserving human stderr outside JSON mode.

Acceptance criteria: - AC1: All current `--json` commands use the same top-level envelope.
- AC2: JSON-mode failures never print human-only text to stdout.
- AC3: Non-JSON failures keep their current human output.
- AC4: `run --json` exposes `report_path`, `id` and the report `status`; it no longer returns captured stdout as a `report` string.
- AC5: In `--json` mode, stdout parses as exactly one JSON object for every command and every outcome, including `EXIT_NO_REPORT`.
- AC6: Selfcheck proves success and failure envelope shape for list, doctor, prune and run.
Problem: - The first `--json` pass made stdout parseable for the common path, but error payloads are not yet consistent across commands and some failures expose only prose.

- `run --json` captures the runner's stdout into a `report` string. The value happens to be the report path today, but the field name says content and the shape says prose: an agent cannot tell which it is holding.

ai_context.keywords: refusal code, unknown operation, missing source, target busy, invalid parameter
ai_context.skip when: changing report warning codes or adding automatic recovery.
ai_context.summary: Add stable refusal codes for the failures agents can recover from without parsing translated prose.
ai_context.use when: mapping runner and CLI refusals to machine-readable error codes.

Acceptance criteria: - AC1: Each named refusal has a stable code in JSON mode.
- AC2: The human message remains present for logs and operators.
- AC3: Codes are documented by `schema cli --json`.
- AC4: Selfcheck covers at least one recovery path per named code without starting Blender.
Problem: - An agent can recover from many refusals, but today it must parse translated text to distinguish missing files, unknown operations, invalid parameters and busy targets.
